items.content_text:
The decisions made at the ballot box can show up in our everyday lives.
 Who makes decisions about your schools?
 Who has a say in healthcare?
 Who decides how public money is spent?
 Who makes the laws that affect your work, your housing, and your community?
 Those decisions are connected to the people and issues on your ballot.
 That’s why it’s not enough to know when to vote. We need to know what and who we’re voting on.
 Before you vote, take some time to learn:
 🗳️ Who’s on your ballot
 🗳️ What office they’re running for
 🗳️ What that office is responsible for
 🗳️ What the candidates have said and done
 🗳️ What each ballot measure would actually change
 The biggest race on your ballot isn’t the only one that matters. Local races and ballot measures can have a direct impact on your community, too.

ArtsBuild Announces 2026–2027 Arts Build Communities Grant Recipients
 ArtsBuild is pleased to announce eight Hamilton County recipients of the Tennessee Arts Commission’s Arts Build Communities (ABC) grants. Administered locally by ArtsBuild, these grants expand access to the arts, strengthen communities, and support creative initiatives.
 Congratulations to this year’s recipients!
 Big Brothers Big Sisters: Collaborative arts workshops connecting youth and mentors with local artists.
 Bridge Builder Collective: The Soundtrack of Chattanooga, empowering students to share their stories through music and art.
 Lookout Comedy: Professional development and entrepreneurship training for Tennessee comedians.
 Next Exit Productions: Myths, a community storytelling project culminating in a free performance on February 25, 2027.
 Scenic City Shakespeare: Free performances of Romeo and Juliet at Greenway Farm Park in May 2027.
 Songbirds Foundation: Afterschool arts education and creative career exploration for middle and high school students.
 University of Tennessee at Chattanooga: Free monthly community writing workshops in partnership with Walnut Street Publishing and Stove Works.
 WauMaus: The Call, transforming CARTA’s downtown parking garage rooftop into an interactive arts and performance space.
 Help keep the arts thriving! Support ArtsBuild’s Annual Campaign and purchase a Tennessee Arts specialty license plate. Specialty plate sales provide approximately 80% of Tennessee’s arts grant funding.
 Donate: [https://artsbuild.com/donate-form](https://artsbuild.com/donate-form) 
 For more information about ArtsBuild grants, visit artsbuild.com or contact Melissa Astin at [melissa@artsbuild.com](mailto:melissa@artsbuild.com).

HCSO Responds to Fatal Single-Vehicle Crash on Birchwood Pike
 Hamilton County, TN – On September 26, at approximately 9 a.m., the Hamilton County Sheriff's Office responded to a vehicle crash at the 11000 block of Birchwood Pike.
 HCSO deputies located a white Dodge Ram partially submerged in a pond with the driver unresponsive inside. The individual was removed from the vehicle, and life-saving measures were initiated; however, EMS pronounced them dead at the scene.
 The HCSO Traffic Unit was notified and responded to the scene to conduct the investigation. The driver's identity will be released pending notification of their next of kin.
 The investigation remains ongoing. This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

What could it cost #OECD countries to prepare for the next pandemic?
 While an uncontrolled outbreak could cost up to 16.2% of GDP, being properly prepared would only cost 6 US dollars per person.
 New OECD analysis highlights three investment priorities:
 ➡️ Stockpiling personal protective equipment and hygiene supplies
 ➡️ Developing capacity to put public health measures in place quickly
 ➡️ Stronger disease surveillance, including wastewater monitoring. These actions could improve everyday health services and pick up other health threats sooner.

Big news from Washington, D.C.! 🏆
 UTC has earned third place and a $150,000 prize in a national U.S. Department of Transportation innovation challenge for PRISM, an AI-powered platform designed to make transportation safer, smarter, and more efficient.
 The UTC-led team rose from 448 submissions nationwide to become one of just four finalists—and the only university-led team to reach the final round.
 Developed by researchers at UTC’s Center for Urban Informatics and Progress, PRISM is already being validated right here in Chattanooga on the MLK Smart Corridor, using real-time transportation data to help vehicles, infrastructure, and transportation operators better understand what’s happening on the road.
 From Chattanooga to the national stage, this is what innovation looks like. 💙💛

items.title: Yesterday, I had the opportunity to deliver the keynote at The ARFF Working Group Educational Symposium in Chattanooga....
items.content_text:
Yesterday, I had the opportunity to deliver the keynote at The ARFF Working Group Educational Symposium in Chattanooga. The keynote was titled “Good Enough Isn’t Enough.”
 We challenged the way minimum standards, which are supposed to establish the floor, can quietly become the ceiling. Over time, simply meeting the standard can become normal, and completion can begin to matter more than actual capability.
 What I did not expect was how familiar everything would feel. Structural firefighting and ARFF may involve different apparatus, hazards, and tactics, but the conversations are the same. We care about our people. We struggle with many of the same cultural and leadership challenges.
 Thank you to the ARFF Working Group for the opportunity and to everyone who took the time to continue the conversation afterward. I went there to challenge others not to settle for good enough, and I left with an even greater appreciation for another part of our fire service.
 #ARFF #FireService #Leadership #Training

Just announced! The Moccasin Bend Roll & Stroll is next Saturday, 9/26! 🎉 
 This event is organized by Chattanooga's Parks and Outdoors with Outdoor Chattanooga, with a ribbon-cutting at 10 Hamm Road (the NPS Gateway Site) and popsicles to be provided afterward at Renaissance Park. 
 Celebrate the addition of another 1.2-miles of greenway to the City's network, providing federal lands connectivity to the Moccasin Bend National Archaeological Site from nearby North Chattanooga. The project highlights the intersection of street safety and public space connections that stem from RPA's 2012 Moccasin Bend Gateway Plan, from the shared-use sidepath being added to the road diet it required along Manufacturers Road and Hamm Road, along with low impact development design strategies, and native plantings that frame the pathway. 
 Join neighbors, families, and outdoor enthusiasts to celebrate more than 10 years of partnerships toward the project between City Departments of Planning, Public Works, and Parks and Outdoors. The ribbon-cutting will be followed by a community trek down the brand-new, safely protected trail straight into Renaissance Park.

items.content_text:
CONGRATS TEAM!
 Hamilton County Breastfeeding Peer Counselors received the 2026 USDA Gold Award of Excellence for exemplary breastfeeding support and practices. The Tennessee Department of Health presented the award during its field staff training on August 27. Hamilton County’s program was one of only three in the state to receive this honor. To qualify, applicants must meet all 30 Gold Award criteria, demonstrating excellence in breastfeeding practices and support beyond the core components of the WIC Breastfeeding Model for Peer Counseling. Hamilton County’s peer counselors are Zina Difrancesco, Paula Allgood, Maricela Martinez, and Exelia Mejia Perez. They provide peer-to-peer education and support to expectant and postpartum mothers throughout their breastfeeding journeys. They are also available after hours to address concerns that may arise. Breastfeeding Coordinator Melissa Johnson, a registered nurse and certified lactation counselor, leads the team and provides specialized assistance to mothers facing a wide range of breastfeeding challenges.

Women working full time across OECD countries still earn, on average, only 90 cents for every dollar or euro earned by men, reflecting a gender wage gap of around 10%. 
 At the current pace of change, achieving equal pay could still take decades. 
 Pay transparency tools have emerged as a promising approach for addressing gender pay gaps by helping to identify pay disparities and support fairer pay practices.

items.content_text:
Chattajack Volunteers Needed :) —Help Bring Chattajack Village to Life!
 The vision for our new finish experience at River Gorge Ranch began nearly two years ago. Now, after months of planning and preparation, we need an incredible volunteer crew to help bring it to life on race day!
 So far, 26 volunteers have stepped forward to support our finish operations—19 at River Gorge Ranch and seven at the OC-6 takeout. We are extremely grateful for every one of them, but we still have 25 volunteer positions available at River Gorge Ranch.
 This will be an exciting and rewarding place to volunteer. You’ll be part of the inaugural Chattajack Village crew, first to welcome racers after their 31-mile journey through the Tennessee River Gorge and helping create the organized, encouraging and memorable experience they deserve.
 Volunteers will help set up and break down tents, organize resources, distribute finisher medals and nutrition, direct racers and their vessels, assist with shuttle loading, and keep everything flowing smoothly throughout the afternoon.
 There are roles for a variety of abilities, including positions that do not require heavy lifting.
 Thank you to the awesome folks who have already signed up as medical volunteers—you are critical to this event! We would love to add a few more, so if you possess medical training, please consider joining Amy Campbell’s amazing medical team. Opportunities are available aboard support boats and at the River Gorge Ranch takeout.
 This is the first year for Chattajack Village, and our volunteers will forever be the crew that helped launch it. We cannot do it without you!
 There's also always that nice CJ vol perk of: anyone who fulfills a Chattajack volunteer role in 2026 receives priority registration for the 2027 race.
 Come share the excitement, support our paddlers and help us create an unforgettable Chattajack experience!
 Sign up here:
 https://www.signupgenius.com/…/4090F48A4AD2EA7F58-65038929-…

 📍 What residents can expect:
 Crews may be working near water meters in the highlighted areas shown on the attached map.
 Small test holes will be excavated to visually inspect service line materials.
 Water service will not be interrupted.
 Any areas disturbed during the work will be restored once the inspection is complete.
 Customers selected for verification will receive advance notification from Tennessee American Water.
 The work is expected to take place over the coming months. Thank you for your patience and cooperation as this important infrastructure work is completed in our community.

items.content_text:
'Ten years ago, the EMC was an experiment. Today, it is a global community of urban leaders united by a shared commitment to making cities more equitable, sustainable and effective.'
 
This weekend, alumni, participants, faculty and invited urban practitioners return to LSE to mark ten years of the EMC and explore the urban questions that shape the programme today and in the future.
 
From the outset, the EMC was an experiment in bringing different forms of urban knowledge and practice into the same learning environment. The people working most directly with cities needed a learning environment equal to the scale and complexity of urban change. Their work cut across public policy, design, development, research, civic life and governance. The programme brought them together to examine the social, spatial, political, environmental and economic forces shaping urban life.
 
That remains the distinctive proposition of the EMC today: a degree that connects professional experience with critical urban research and allows participants to test ideas against the realities of other cities and forms of practice.
 
At this weekend’s Anniversary Forum, we will discuss themes that have been central to the EMC since its launch, including social inclusion, the urban environment, economic development and governance. The occasion brings the community back into conversation around the pressures now facing cities and the ways urban practice is changing in response.
 
The next decade of urban leadership will be shaped by climate risk, housing affordability, technological change, democratic pressure, fiscal constraint and new forms of institutional innovation.
 
Responding to those pressures will require city leaders and urban practitioners with the skills, judgement and perspective to work across disciplines, sectors and places, and make better decisions for cities. By connecting professional experience from across the globe with teaching grounded in critical urban research, the EMC today remains more relevant than ever.
 
Read more about how the EMC took shape and has developed here: https://lnkd.in/efgi4p64

Having a baby. Moving home. Applying for a permit. These everyday life events often require people to interact with multiple public services.
 The Serving Citizens 2026 report explores how governments across #OECD and partner countries  organise and deliver public administrative services, and what more can be done to put people at the centre.
 It's the first overview of human-centred public administrative services across OECD countries.Key findings include
 ➡️ 87% of OECD countries have a strategy to improve public administrative services
 ➡️ 55% use people's feedback to  improve services
 ➡️ Just 20% ofcommon life events are supported by integrated services across different public agencies
 The report highlights practical ways governments can deliver services that are more connected, proactive and human-centred through digitalisation, cross-government collaboration, stronger service design capabilities and greater use of user satisfaction data.
 Read the report: https://brnw.ch/21x5X92

items.content_text:
🎺🥁 What a night for HCS marching bands! 🎶

Red Bank High School hosted the inaugural Hamilton County Marching Band Exhibition Tuesday night, bringing together marching bands from across Hamilton County for an evening full of music, school spirit and community!

Students from Soddy Daisy, Sale Creek, Hixson, Tyner, East Hamilton, Central, Signal Mountain, Ooltewah, Brainerd and Red Bank high schools, along with the UTC Marching Mocs, took the field to showcase the hard work and dedication they’ve put into their programs. 👏

The exhibition was about more than performances — it was a chance for students, families and band programs to come together, cheer each other on and celebrate the marching arts across our community. 💙

A special thank-you to Red Bank for hosting this exciting event! Proceeds will support the Red Bank Band as they prepare to represent Hamilton County and Chattanooga in the Fiesta Bowl Parade in Phoenix later this year. 🌵🎉

items.title: The Tri-State Mutual Aid Association will host a two-day swiftwater rescue training event, bringing together regional em...
items.content_text:
The Tri-State Mutual Aid Association will host a two-day swiftwater rescue training event, bringing together regional emergency response teams to refine critical water rescue skills and enhance multi-agency coordination.
 The exercise on September 29-30, 2026 will take place on the Ocoee River. Hamilton County Special Tactics & Rescue Services (STARS), the Chattanooga Fire Department, and the Cleveland Fire Department are involved, in conjunction with Ocoee River State Park, TVA, and the US Forest Service. 
 Training evolutions will run throughout both days. Participating swiftwater rescue personnel will rotate through multiple high-intensity hands-on skills stations. 
 Training together on the water ensures swiftwater teams speak the same operational language, align safety protocols, and build the seamless trust required when combining forces during critical rescue operations. The Chattanooga Fire Fighters Association Local 820, Big Woody’s Tree Service, and Morning Pointe Senior Living have been strong supporters of this fantastic learning opportunity and we appreciate their partnership.

items.content_text:
Brian Freeman’s 42-year journey toward a degree wasn’t a matter of if, but of when, and he learned that the journey itself matters.
 Freeman credits UTC support for helping him reach his upcoming graduation in December 2026. He has spent the past two semesters working toward it through the Leadership and Learning (LEAP) program.
 “If it wasn’t for UTC and the support systems—from the IT to the counseling, to the Studio, the writing clinics, math labs—everything is undergirded,” Freeman said. “I mean, it’s not impossible for you to fail, but there are so many safety measures to catch you, and I’ve taken advantage of all that.”
 🔗  Read more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/for-brian-freeman-the-work-is-the-r…/
